scope: Authentic public documentation downloaded for this review, not customer responses or Production verification. Examples remain illustrative and do not authorize submission. No credentials, live lock or remittance were used.

legacy_lock.description: Fetches the exchange rate for a currency pair and locks and holds the rate until the expiry time returned in the response. Use it before calling the Transfer Money API, passing the returned auditId in the payout (the field name can be passed as either `auditId` or `audit_id`). Requires the source currency and destination currency, and optionally an additional FX markup. Returns the auditId, FX rate, markup rate, ECB exchange rate, hold expiry time and status of the locked rate. **Note:** The auditId is valid only for the same client, customer and wallet, and only until it expires.

parameters.name: sourceCurrency
parameters.description: The [3-letter ISO-4217 currency code](/docs/getting-started/currency-and-country-codes) for the source amount.

parameters.name: additionalFxMarkup
parameters.description: This field is used if client wants to apply additional Fxmarkup in the exchange rate for their customer. The value should be in percentage. For example use 0.10 for 0.1% additional markup.

referenced_destination_parameter.description: The [3-letter ISO-4217 currency code](/docs/getting-started/currency-and-country-codes) for the destination amount.
referenced_destination_parameter.name: destinationCurrency

additionalFxMarkup.description: The Additional Fx Markup of the given audit ID

audit_id.description: The audit ID which is generated by Nium as a unique number for internal purposes. Pass this value as `auditId` or `audit_id` in the payout object of the Transfer Money request; both field names are supported.

destination_currency.description: The 3-letter [ISO-4217 destination currency code](/docs/getting-started/currency-and-country-codes) for the destination amount.

fx_rate.description: Effective FX rate after deducting the `markup_rate`.

hold_expiry_at.description:
The timestamp until the exchange rate will be valid. 
In other words, the timestamp at which the exchange rate held by Nium shall expire. In the `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ` format.

markup_rate.description: The markup rate charged by Nium.

source_currency.description: The 3-letter [ISO-4217 source currency code](/docs/getting-started/currency-and-country-codes) for the source amount.

status.description: The status of the given audit ID

Default.summary: Exchange rate locked for SGD to USD transfer with 1-hour hold

remittance.description: Sends money from a customer's wallet to a registered beneficiary or recipient. For more information, see [Transfer Money](/docs/payouts/transfer-money). Use it after the beneficiary is registered, and optionally after validating the request with the Validate Transfer Money API or locking a rate with the [Create Quote](/api#tag/quotes/POST/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/quotes) API. Requires a registered beneficiary, a payout source currency that is held in the wallet with the amount, a customer with Clear status, and a wallet balance that covers the amount and fees (unless your client is post-funded); send an x-idempotency-id header to safely retry. Initiates the payout and returns the systemReferenceNumber and a message. **Note:** Track the payout with the Fetch Remittance Life Cycle Status API.

illustrative_local_example.summary: Send money using a local payout

id.description: This is an unique beneficiary ID which depends upon the destination currency and payout method. The beneficiary Id and payout ID can be found out using [Beneficiary List](/baas/beneficiary-list) API.

payout.description: This object accepts the payout details.

auditId.description:
The audit Id must be taken from [Exchange Rate Lock and Hold](/baas/exchange-rate-lock-and-hold) API.
Note: This field name can also be passed as `audit_id`.

destinationAmount.description:
Accepts the destination amount for remittance. Either the source or the destination amount is mandatory.

Allowed decimal limit is 2.
Note: This field name can also be passed as destination_amount.

preScreening.description: Details if compliance checks are to be done at the time of payout creation. This field is applicable only for scheduled and Post-Funded payouts.

quoteId.description:
The FX quote id must be obtained from the [Create Quote](/api#tag/quotes/POST/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/quotes) API, used as an alternative to auditId.
Note: This field name can also be passed as quote_id. Mutually exclusive with auditId.

scheduledPayoutDate.description: This field accepts scheduled payout date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format

serviceTime.description: The date of providing of service/export in yyyy-MM-dd format

sourceAmount.description:
Accepts the source amount for remittance. Either the source or the destination amount is mandatory.

Allowed decimal limit is 2.
Note: This field name can also be passed as source_amount.

sourceCurrency.description:
Accepts the source currency for remittance.
Note: This field name can also be passed as source_currency.

swiftFeeType.description:
This field accepts the swift fee type and defines who will bear the SWIFT charges for the given transaction. Clients can send any of the below values basis which, they will be charged for the SWIFT transaction. In case this field is absent SHA will be applied by default.

OUR - SWIFT charges borne by the customer
SHA - SWIFT charges shared by the customer and beneficiary

Note: Clients should make sure that fee template is configured for each of the swift fee type. To know if the template is configured, clients should call [Fee Details](/apis/reference/feedetails) API

tradeOrderID.description: This field should denote the invoice number relevant to the transaction

estimatedDeliveryTime.description: This field is estimated delivery time of transaction.

message.description: This field will return a success message if the money transferred successfully.

systemReferenceNumber.description: This is a unique system reference number assigned to the transaction.

system_reference_number.description: This is a unique system reference number assigned to the transaction.

payout_schema.description: This API allows you to fetch the payout validation schema.

parameters.name: destinationCountry
parameters.description: This field accepts the destination country.

guides.verbatim_section:
# Singapore Payments - SGD

URL: https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/country-and-regional-guides/sgd-payments-to-singapore

Send SGD payouts to bank accounts and PayNow proxies in Singapore using FAST, MEPS+, PayNow, and GIRO.

Singapore operates one of the most advanced payment infrastructures in Asia. FAST (Fast and Secure Transfers) enables real-time 24/7 bank-to-bank payments up to 200,000 SGD, PayNow extends this with proxy-based transfers using everyday identifiers such as mobile numbers, UEN, NRIC, or FIN, and MEPS+ (MAS Electronic Payment System) provides real-time gross settlement for high-value transactions with no upper limit. Together, these rails give clients comprehensive coverage of Singapore domestic payment needs across all value segments across various use cases.

The payout methods below are available through the existing [TransferMoney API](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/payout/POST/api/v1/client/%7BclientHashId%7D/customer/%7BcustomerHashId%7D/wallet/%7BwalletHashId%7D/remittance). The primary change between methods is the `payout_method` value and the required fields for the target rail. NIUM handles rail selection, amount-based routing, and real-time status updates automatically. Refer to [Payout Rail Preference](https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/transfer-money/payout-rail-preference) if you are interested in selecting the payout rail. For up-to-date corridor capabilities, see the [Singapore Playbook](https://playbook.nium.com/country/Singapore).

## Supported Payment Methods

| Feature               | FAST                                      | MEPS+                                            | PayNow                                    | GIRO                                                                                                | SWIFT               |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| **Payout Method**     | `LOCAL`                                   | `LOCAL`                                          | `PROXY`                                   | `LOCAL` (automatic fallback)                                                                        | `SWIFT`             |
| **Use Case**          | Bank account, real-time up to 200,000 SGD | Bank account, RTGS for amounts above 200,000 SGD | Proxy-based via mobile, UEN, NRIC, or FIN | Fallback for high-value transactions outside MEPS hours or when beneficiary address is not provided | International wires |
| **Delivery**          | Realtime (24/7/365)                       | Near Real time subject to cutoff (business days) | Realtime (24/7/365)                       | Next business day                                                                                   | 1-2 business days   |
| **Cutoff**            | 24x7                                      | 19:00 SGT (Mon-Fri, excluding public holidays)   | 24x7                                      | 13:30 SGT                                                                                           | Business days only  |
| **Transaction Limit** | 1 to 200,000 SGD                          | Above 200,000 SGD (no upper cap)                 | 1 to 200,000 SGD                          | Above 200,000 SGD                                                                                   | No fixed limit      |
| **Routing Code**      | SWIFT BIC                                 | SWIFT BIC                                        | Not required                              | SWIFT BIC                                                                                           | SWIFT BIC           |

## Bank Account Payouts

When you send a bank account payout (`payout_method = LOCAL`) in SGD, NIUM automatically routes it based on the transaction amount and the fields you provide. You do not need to specify a rail.

- **Up to 200,000 SGD** — Routes via FAST. Funds settle in seconds, 24/7.
- **Above 200,000 SGD, submitted on a business day before 19:00 SGT, with** `beneficiary_address` and `beneficiary_city` included — Routes via MEPS+ (RTGS). Funds settle in near real time.
- **Above 200,000 SGD, submitted outside MEPS hours, or if** `beneficiary_address` or `beneficiary_city` is missing — Falls back to GIRO. Funds settle on the next business day, subject to a 13:30 SGT cutoff.

To consistently get MEPS+ for high-value transactions, always include `beneficiary_address` and `beneficiary_city` in your request.

### Required Fields - Bank Account Payouts

The table below covers fields that have SGD-specific requirements or affect rail routing. For the full list of required fields, refer to the [TransferMoney API Reference](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/payout/POST/api/v1/client/%7BclientHashId%7D/customer/%7BcustomerHashId%7D/wallet/%7BwalletHashId%7D/remittance).

| Field                  | Required    | Validation                      | Notes                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `payout_method`        | Yes         | `LOCAL`                         |                                                                                                                        |
| `destination_currency` | Yes         | `SGD`                           |                                                                                                                        |
| `destination_amount`   | Yes         | Min 1 SGD, max 2 decimal places |                                                                                                                        |
| `routing_code_type_1`  | Yes         | `SWIFT CODE`                    | SWIFT BIC of the receiving bank                                                                                        |
| `beneficiary_address`  | Conditional | Max 255 characters              | Required for MEPS+ routing. If not provided, transactions above 200,000 SGD will fall back to GIRO (next business day) |
| `beneficiary_city`     | Conditional | Max 50 characters               | Required for MEPS+ routing. If not provided, transactions above 200,000 SGD will fall back to GIRO (next business day) |
| `remit_purpose_code`   | Yes         | Valid NIUM purpose code         | See [Purpose Codes](https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/transfer-money/purpose-codes)                                   |

### Payout Lifecycle

SGD payouts follow the standard remittance lifecycle with additional SGD-specific status updates.

| Step | Status                                                                                                                                          | Description                                                                                                                 | Step type        |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| 1    | `SCHEDULED``AWAITING_FUNDS``CANCELLED``EXPIRED``FAILED``INITIATED``RFI_REQUESTED``RFI_RESPONDED``COMPLIANCE_COMPLETED``REJECTED``PG_PROCESSING` | Standard payout lifecycle statuses. For definitions, see [Track Payouts](https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/track-payouts). | Generic          |
| 2    | `SENT_TO_BANK`                                                                                                                                  | The payment has been submitted to the FAST, MEPS+, or GIRO network for processing.                                          | Country-specific |
| 3    | `PAID`                                                                                                                                          | The beneficiary has been credited — in real time for FAST and MEPS+, or on the next business day for GIRO.                  | Country-specific |
| 4    | `RETURN`                                                                                                                                        | The payout was returned by the receiving bank, for example due to an invalid account number or closed account.              | Country-specific |

Webhooks and transaction status enquiry work the same for all SGD payout methods. For more information, see [Payout Lifecycle](https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/track-payouts#payout-lifecycle).

## PayNow (Proxy Payouts)

PayNow is Singapore's national payment alias system. It lets individuals and businesses register a mobile number, UEN, NRIC, or FIN as a payment alias linked to their bank account. You provide only the identifier — NIUM resolves it to the underlying account and routes the payment in real time.

This means you do not need to collect bank account numbers or routing codes from your payees. PayNow payouts settle in seconds, 24/7, and are well-suited for consumer disbursements, gig economy payouts, and B2B payments to SMEs with a registered UEN. If the proxy identifier is not registered or has been deregistered, the transaction fails before funds are moved.

### Proxy Types and Format

| Proxy Type    | `proxy_type` value | Format                                                                                                                        | Example       |
| ------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Mobile number | `MOBILE`           | Country code +65 followed by 8 digits. The local number must begin with 8 or 9                                                | `+6581234567` |
| UEN           | `UEN`              | 9 or 10 alphanumeric characters issued by ACRA. Format varies by entity type                                                  | `201912345A`  |
| NRIC          | `NRIC`             | 1 letter (S or T) followed by 7 digits and 1 check letter. S-series for citizens born before 2000, T-series from 2000 onwards | `S1234567D`   |
| FIN           | `FIN`              | 1 letter (F or G) followed by 7 digits and 1 check letter. Issued to foreign residents holding Singapore long-term passes     | `F1234567N`   |

### Required Fields - PayNow

The table below covers fields specific to PayNow. For the full list of required fields, refer to the [TransferMoney API Reference](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/payout/POST/api/v1/client/%7BclientHashId%7D/customer/%7BcustomerHashId%7D/wallet/%7BwalletHashId%7D/remittance).

| Field                  | Required | Validation                        | Notes                            |
| ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `payout_method`        | Yes      | `PROXY`                           |                                  |
| `destination_currency` | Yes      | `SGD`                             |                                  |
| `destination_amount`   | Yes      | 1 to 200,000 SGD                  |                                  |
| `proxy_type`           | Yes      | `MOBILE`, `UEN`, `NRIC`, or `FIN` |                                  |
| `proxy_value`          | Yes      | Max 255 characters                | The registered PayNow identifier |

## Return Codes

The following ISO return codes are the most common errors observed for SGD transactions.

| ISO Code | Reason                          | Resolution                                                                                |
| -------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AC03`   | Invalid creditor account number | Verify the beneficiary account number and SWIFT BIC. Confirm both belong to the same bank |
| `AC04`   | Closed account number           | Request updated account details from the beneficiary. Covers expired and closed accounts  |
| `AM03`   | Not allowed currency            | Contact Nium support. This indicates a routing configuration issue                        |

## Related Resources

- [TransferMoney API Reference](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/payout/POST/api/v1/client/%7BclientHashId%7D/customer/%7BcustomerHashId%7D/wallet/%7BwalletHashId%7D/remittance)
- [Track Payouts - Status Definitions](https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/track-payouts)
- [Purpose Codes](https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/transfer-money/purpose-codes)
- [Payout Webhook Events](https://docs.nium.com/docs/developers/notifications-and-webhooks/payout-events/remit-transaction-paid)

---

# Transfer Money

URL: https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/transfer-money

You can create payouts to transfer funds using one of the following methods:

- [Pre-created beneficiary](#pre-created-beneficiary)
- [Inline beneficiary details](#inline-beneficiary)
- [Batch upload](#batch-upload)
- [Batch API](#bulk-api)

Select the method based on payout frequency, operational workflow, and automation requirements.

## Payout methods

### Pre-created beneficiary

Create a beneficiary once and reuse it across multiple payouts. We recommend pre-creating a beneficiary when you need to create recurring payouts.

This reduces payload size, avoids repeated validation, and improves operational consistency.

#### Step 1: Create a beneficiary

Use the [Create Beneficiary](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/beneficiary/POST/api/v2/client/{clientHashId}/customer/{customerHashId}/beneficiaries) request.

This returns a `beneficiaryHashId` that uniquely identifies the beneficiary.

Store the `beneficiaryHashId` for future use.

#### Step 2: Create a payout referencing the beneficiary

Use the [Create Payout (Remittance)](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/payout/POST/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/customer/{customerHashId}/wallet/{walletHashId}/remittance) request.

Include the stored `beneficiaryHashId` in the request body:

```json
{
  "beneficiary": {
    "id": "6081219f04fa070017d12e68"
  },
  "payout": {
    "destinationAmount": 10
  },
  "purposeCode": "IR005"
}
```

Use this method for payroll, vendor payments, marketplace disbursements, and other recurring payouts.

### Inline beneficiary

Include beneficiary details directly in the payout request without pre-creating a beneficiary. We recommend creating beneficiaries inline when you need to create one-time payouts.

No beneficiary record is stored.

Use the [Create Payout (Remittance)](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/payout/POST/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/customer/{customerHashId}/wallet/{walletHashId}/remittance) request and include all beneficiary details inline:

```json
{
  "beneficiary": {
    "beneficiary": {
      "name": "John Doe",
      "accountType": "CORPORATE"
    },
    "paymentAccount": {
      "accountNumber": "1234567",
      "payoutMethod": "LOCAL",
      "payoutCurrency": "INR",
      "routingCode": [
        {
          "type": "IFSC CODE",
          "value": "ICIC0001451"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "payout": {
    "destinationAmount": 10
  },
  "purposeCode": "IR005"
}
```

Use this method for ad-hoc or infrequent transfers when you do not need to reuse a beneficiary.

### Batch upload

Submit multiple payouts using a CSV file through Nium Portal.

This method is suitable for finance-led workflows and spreadsheet-based processes.

- Upload a CSV file in Nium Portal
- Validate file rows
- Execute the payout batch

For more information, see [Batch Payout](https://docs.nium.com/docs/nium-portal/batch-payouts#create-a-batch-payout).

### Batch payout API

Submit up to 1,000 payouts in a single API request. We recommend using the Batch Payout request when you need to automate a high volume of payouts.

This method is designed for automated platforms, marketplaces, and large-scale payout orchestration.

Use the [Create Batch Payout](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/bulk-payouts) request.

Features of the Batch endpoint include:

- Per-item status tracking
- Bulk-level lifecycle tracking
- Webhook notifications
- Scheduled execution (`executeAt`)
- Idempotency support

Each batch can:

- Reference a pre-created beneficiary, or
- Include inline beneficiary details

Use this method when building automated disbursement systems.

## Create quote

If currency conversion is required prior to payout, use the [Create Quote](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/conversions/POST/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/customer/{customerHashId}/wallet/{walletHashId}/conversions) request to convert and then initiate payout request.

If you intend to lock a rate and use for multiple payouts, use the [Create Quote](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/quotes/POST/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/quotes) request with `quoteType` as `payout`.

Pass the returned quote `id` as the `quoteId` when creating the payout. You can use the same quote for several payouts until its `expiryTime`. For details, see [Locked Rate for Payouts](https://docs.nium.com/docs/foreign-exchange/locked-rate-payouts).

## Upload documents

If compliance requires additional documentation, use the [Upload Payout Document](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/payouts/POST/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/customer/{customerHashId}/wallet/{walletHashId}/transactions/{transactionId}/receipt) request.

Documentation requirements vary by corridor and payout type.

## Payout comparison

| Requirement                   | Recommended Method      |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| One-time payout               | Inline beneficiary      |
| Recurring payout              | Pre-created beneficiary |
| Manual spreadsheet workflow   | Batch upload            |
| High-volume automated payouts | Batch endpoint          |

## Validation errors

If a payout request contains missing or invalid fields, a structured validation error response is returned.

This response helps you identify which field caused the error and how to resolve it.

Validation errors follow a unified schema.

### Response body

| Field         | Description                                                          |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`        | Machine-readable error identifier describing the validation failure. |
| `description` | Human-readable explanation of the error.                             |
| `field`       | The request field that caused the error.                             |
| `action`      | Recommended action to resolve the issue.                             |
| `regex`       | Validation pattern required for the field, when applicable.          |

### Example response

If a payout request is submitted without a beneficiary address, the response can return:

```json
{
  "code": "field_missing",
  "description": "Field is missing",
  "field": "beneficiary.address",
  "action": "Input the beneficiary address",
  "regex": "^.[A-Za-z0-9 -.]{1,255}$"
}
```

This response indicates that the `beneficiary.address` field was not provided and must be included in the request.

### Legacy schema

Newly onboarded customers receive validation errors using the error schema shown above.

Some existing integrations may continue to receive validation errors in a previous response format. This does not affect existing integrations.

Legacy integrations can adopt the new error schema to use the standardized error structure shown in this section.

### Handling validation errors

When building payout integrations, consider the following best practices:

- Logging the returned error response
- Mapping `code` values to retry or correction logic
- Displaying the `description` or `action` message in internal dashboards or operational tools
- Validating required fields before submitting payout requests when possible

Handling validation errors correctly helps reduce failed payout attempts and improves operational reliability.

## Lifecycle and status tracking

After creating a payout:

- Retrieve status using the Get Transaction endpoint
- Subscribe to webhook events for real-time updates
- Handle returned or rejected transactions if applicable
- Upload additional documentation if requested

See our [Payout Webhooks](https://docs.nium.com/docs/developers/notifications-and-webhooks/payout-events) documentation for event schemas and status transitions.

See [Track Payouts](https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/track-payouts) for details on how to track payouts.

---

# Payout Validation Schema

URL: https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/transfer-money/payout-validation-schema

Fetch the required fields, validation rules, and purpose codes for a payout corridor before you submit a payout.

The **Payout Validation Schema** request returns every required field, validation rule, and constraint for a payout. You filter the result by destination country, currency, and payout method.

Instead of relying on static documentation, you can programmatically discover the exact data a payout needs before you submit it. This reduces rejected transactions and shortens your integration time.

## Benefits

- **One request for all corridors:** Get field-level requirements for any supported corridor.
- **Filtered results:** Query by destination country, currency, and payout method.
- **Per-field rules:** See whether a field is required, its accepted format, length limits, and allowed values.
- **Purpose codes:** Get the corridor-specific values accepted in the `purposeCode` field.
- **Dynamic validation:** Build your payout form and validate your payload once, instead of fixing errors through trial and error in UAT.

## How it works

1. Before you create a payout, call the [Payout Validation Schema](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/payout/GET/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/customer/{customerHashId}/currency/{currencyCode}/payout/schema) request with the destination currency, destination country, and payout method.
2. Read the returned schema to find the fields your request must include, along with their validation rules.
3. Use the schema to build your payout form or validate your request payload.
4. Optionally, check the complete payload with the [Payout Validator](https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/transfer-money/payment-validator) request.
5. Submit the payout using the [Transfer Money](https://docs.nium.com/docs/payouts/transfer-money) request.

## API request

```http
GET /api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/customer/{customerHashId}/currency/USD/payout/schema?payoutMethod=SWIFT&destinationCountry=US
x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
x-request-id: YOUR_UNIQUE_UUID
```

### Path parameters

| Parameter        | Required | Description                                                           |
| ---------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `clientHashId`   | Yes      | Unique client identifier generated and shared before API handshake.   |
| `customerHashId` | Yes      | Unique customer identifier generated on customer creation.            |
| `currencyCode`   | Yes      | Destination currency as a 3-letter ISO 4217 code, for example, `PHP`. |

### Query parameters

| Parameter            | Required | Description                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `payoutMethod`       | Yes      | The payout method. Accepted values: `LOCAL`, `SWIFT`, `PROXY`, `WALLET`, `CARD`, `CASH`, and `CHECK`. |
| `destinationCountry` | Yes      | Destination country as a 2-letter ISO 3166 alpha-2 code, for example, `PH`.                           |

## Response

The response is a [JSON Schema (draft 2020-12)](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12) document for the requested corridor. You can pass it to any standard JSON Schema validator library to validate your payout payload.

Each property name is the dot-notation path to a field in your payout request. For example, `beneficiary.paymentAccount.accountNumber` refers to the `accountNumber` field inside the beneficiary's `paymentAccount` object.

The following example shows the response for a local PHP payout to the Philippines:

Example response: PHP local payout schema

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "unified.php.local.json",
  "type": "object",
  "title": "PHP Local Unified Schema",
  "required": [
    "beneficiary.paymentAccount.payoutCurrency",
    "payout.destinationAmount",
    "remitter.name",
    "remitter.accountType",
    "remitter.address",
    "remitter.countryCode",
    "remitter.identificationType",
    "remitter.identificationNumber",
    "beneficiary.beneficiary.name",
    "beneficiary.beneficiary.addresses[0].line1",
    "beneficiary.beneficiary.addresses[0].countryCode",
    "beneficiary.beneficiary.accountType",
    "beneficiary.paymentAccount.accountNumber",
    "beneficiary.paymentAccount.routingCode[0].type",
    "beneficiary.paymentAccount.routingCode[0].value",
    "beneficiary.paymentAccount.payoutMethod",
    "payout.sourceCurrency"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "beneficiary.paymentAccount.payoutCurrency": {
      "$id": "/properties/beneficiary.paymentAccount.payoutCurrency",
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Destination Currency",
      "const": "PHP",
      "description": "Destination currency should be PHP"
    },
    "payout.destinationAmount": {
      "$id": "/properties/payout.destinationAmount",
      "type": "number",
      "title": "Destination Amount",
      "maximumDecimals": 2,
      "minimum": 0.01,
      "description": "Destination Amount should be minimum 0.01 PHP and upto two decimal places are allowed."
    },
    "customerComments": {
      "$id": "/properties/customerComments",
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Statement Narrative",
      "pattern": "^[a-zA-Z0-9_\\s]{0,255}$",
      "description": "Statement narrative can contain only these special characters - (_). Length should not be more than 255 characters."
    },
    "remitter.name": {
      "$id": "/properties/remitter.name",
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Remitter Name",
      "pattern": "^[A-Za-z0-9 .,()_'/&-]{1,100}$",
      "description": "Remitter Name can contain only these special characters - (. , ( ) _ ' / &-). Length should not be more than 100 characters."
    },
    "remitter.accountType": {
      "$id": "/properties/remitter.accountType",
      "title": "Remitter Account Type",
```

| Keyword                      | Description                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `required`                   | Fields that your payout request must include for this corridor.                                     |
| `properties`                 | The rules for each field, keyed by the field's dot-notation path.                                   |
| `type`                       | The data type of the field, such as `string` or `number`.                                           |
| `pattern`                    | A regular expression that the field value must match.                                               |
| `maxLength`                  | The maximum length of a string field.                                                               |
| `minimum`, `maximumDecimals` | The smallest accepted amount and the maximum number of decimal places.                              |
| `enum`                       | The list of accepted values for the field.                                                          |
| `const`                      | The only accepted value for the field.                                                              |
| `description`                | A readable explanation of the field's rules.                                                        |
| `allOf` with `if` and `then` | Conditional rules. When the `if` condition matches your request, the rules under `then` also apply. |

In the example, the `allOf` block contains two kinds of conditional rules:

- **Additional required fields:** When `payout.destinationAmount` is 500,001 PHP or more, `sourceOfFunds` and `purposeCode` also become required.
- **Accepted purpose codes:** The accepted `purposeCode` values depend on the combination of `remitter.accountType` and `beneficiary.beneficiary.accountType`. For example, when both are `INDIVIDUAL`, `purposeCode` must be one of the listed `IR` codes.

# Fees

URL: https://docs.nium.com/docs/fees-and-limits/fees

When processing payments, fees and foreign exchange (FX) margins get applied to client transactions (customer transactions for platform clients), including payouts and account openings.

When processing payments, **fees** and **foreign exchange (FX) margins** get applied to client transactions (customer transactions for platform clients), including payouts and account openings.

Nium’s pricing engine supports a wide range of customizable pricing options through fees and FX margins, including, but not limited to:

- Pricing based on payout or payin method
- Tiered pricing structures

Fees and FX margins are typically applied in the following scenarios:

- **Real-time fee**: Charged at the time of the transaction.
  - For example, when a payout is processed, the corresponding fee (and any FX margin) is debited from the customer's wallet along with the transaction amount.

- **One-time fee**: Charged when a one-off event occurs.
  - For example, a customer may be charged after completeing onboarding.

- **Custom fee**: Charged for events outside the standard pricing model.
  - For example, a client may charge a monthly subscription fee or a fee based on the inbound payment method. Use the [Charge Fee](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/customer-fees/POST/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/customer/{customerHashId}/wallet/{walletHashId}/fees) request to apply a custom fee to a customer’s wallet in any supported currency. Custom fees follow the same processing and accounting logic as predefined fees and can be included in the client’s regular invoicing.

For the above events, pricing is configured in the client's account once mutually agreed upon with Nium during onboarding.

- **FI clients** – Fees are charged to the FI client for real-time and one-time transactions.
- **Direct clients** – Fees are charged to the client for real-time and one-time transactions.
- **Platform clients** – Fees are charged to the platform client's customers. Clients can define customer segments during onboarding and configure pricing by segment. For example, high-volume customers may have different rates than low-volume customers.

Use the [Fee Details](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/client-settings/GET/api/v2/client/{clientHashId}/fees) request to review the real-time transaction pricing.

For additional details, see [Pricing details](#pricing-details).

- Before charging any customer fees, you must obtain approval from Nium’s legal and compliance teams.
- Do **not** use the [Charge Fee](https://docs.nium.com/api#tag/customer-fees/POST/api/v1/client/{clientHashId}/customer/{customerHashId}/wallet/{walletHashId}/fees) request without explicit approval.
- For more information, reach out to your Nium account manager or [Nium Support](mailto:support@nium.com).

## Pricing components

Nium’s *pricing engine* consists of the following key components:

- **Plan name**: Defines the pricing configuration for a customer segment, assigned during onboarding.
- **Product name**: Specifies the product the fee applies to. Supported products include payouts, payins, accounts, FX, cards, and verify.
- **Fee name**: Predefined fee that is automatically applied when specific transaction events occur.
- **Rules**: Conditions that determine when a fee is applied. Rules can be based on transaction volume, amount, or quantity. For example, a rule might apply a fee only if the transaction’s source currency is `USD`.
- **Fees**: The amount charged for a given event, defined as either a flat fee or a percentage-based fee. For example, a transaction with `USD` as the source currency might be charged a flat fee of 1 USD.

## Pre-defined fees

The following table lists the available **pre-defined fees** and **FX margin** types, along with their descriptions and when they are charged.

### Payouts

The following fees are charged on a per-transaction basis.

| Fee name                     | Description                                                                                      | **Real-time or One-time** |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| **REMIT_BANK_FEE**           | Charged on remittance transactions when `payoutMethod` is **LOCAL**.                             | Real-time                 |
| **REMIT_BANK_FEE_SWIFT**     | Charged on remittance transactions when `payoutType` is **SWIFT** and `swiftFeeType` is **SHA**. | Real-time                 |
| **REMIT_BANK_FEE_SWIFT_BEN** | Charged on remittance transactions when `payoutType` is **SWIFT** and `swiftFeeType` is **BEN**. | Real-time                 |
| **REMIT_BANK_FEE_SWIFT_OUR** | Charged on remittance transactions when `payoutType` is **SWIFT** and `swiftFeeType` is **OUR**. | Real-time                 |
| **REMIT_CARD_FEE**           | Charged on remittance transactions when `payoutType` is **CARD**.                                | Real-time                 |

## Real-time transactions

When a fee or FX margin is charged during a real-time transaction, a separate transaction type called **Fee_Debit** is created.

If the transaction is later reversed, a second transaction type, **Fee_Reversal**, is created. The **Fee_Reversal** object includes the following details:

- **feeFixedOrPercentage**: Indicates if the fee is a flat amount or a percentage.
- **feeTransactionCurrency**: Currency in which the fee was charged.
- **exchangeRate**: If the fee was charged in a different currency than configured, this shows the FX rate used to calculate the converted fee.
- **feeAuthCurrency**: Currency used during the transaction’s authorization process.
- **feeName**: Name of the fee applied.
- **feeValueCurrency**: Currency in which the fee is defined (before conversion).
- **feeSlab**: For tiered pricing, identifies the pricing tier applied to the transaction.
- **feeValue**: Amount charged as the fee.
